question: What is the main goal of barrier nursing in a hospital ward?

options.A: To speed up patient physical rehabilitation
options.B: To cure chronic non-communicable diseases quickly
options.C: To reduce the cost of hospital admissions
options.D: To prevent the spread of infectious pathogens

explanation: You've got this! Barrier nursing simply uses physical blocks like gowns and gloves to stop germs from jumping between patients and staff. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h1)

question: Why do we use physical barriers when caring for infectious patients?

options.A: They eliminate the need to administer antibiotics
options.B: They completely sterilize the immediate patient environment
options.C: They stop microorganisms from reaching susceptible hosts
options.D: They replace the need for hand hygiene entirely

explanation: Think of it as putting a shield up! Physical barriers block the path so germs can't travel to people who could easily get sick. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h1)

question: Which link in the chain of infection do you break every time you wash your hands properly?
explanation: Handwashing is your superpower! It washes away germs before they can travel from surfaces or people to someone else. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: A patient comes in with a surgical wound. In the chain of infection, what does this wound represent?
explanation: Spot on! When the skin is open, it gives outside germs a direct doorway straight into the body's tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: What type of isolation protects a weak, immunocompromised patient from outside infections?
explanation: Great thinking! Protective isolation acts like a safety bubble around vulnerable patients who can't fight off everyday germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: A patient is confirmed to have Lassa fever. Which category of barrier nursing do they need?
explanation: High-risk infections like Lassa fever need strict isolation to keep both the hospital and the community safe and sound. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: To which patients should standard precautions be applied in the clinical setting?

options.C: Patients admitted to the surgical ward only
options.D: Only patients with confirmed viral infections

explanation: Always treat every patient as if their body fluids could carry germs. Safety first for everyone, every time! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h4)

question: When should you start transmission-based precautions for a patient?

options.A: During routine morning vital sign checks
options.B: When an infection is suspected or confirmed
options.C: Only after the patient is discharged home
options.D: Before the patient enters the hospital gate

explanation: You start these extra precautions the moment doctors or nurses suspect a specific bug is trying to spread. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h4)

question: When taking off your protective gear (doffing), which item should you remove FIRST?
explanation: Your gloves carry the most germs, so peeling them off first keeps your hands clean for the rest of the steps! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h5)

question: Why is following the correct sequence for putting on protective gear so important?

options.A: It makes the removal process completely unnecessary
options.B: It ensures the nurse looks professional to visitors
options.C: It reduces the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: It prevents self-contamination during the preparation process

explanation: Doing things in the right order ensures you don't accidentally spread germs to your clean skin or uniform. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h5)

question: What color of waste bag is normally used for infectious clinical waste?
explanation: Yellow means go with caution! Yellow bags are reserved for infectious medical waste that needs safe disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: Why must we sort and throw away clinical waste immediately at the spot where it is generated?

options.A: To prevent accidental injuries and cross-contamination
options.B: To eliminate the need for surface disinfection
options.C: To make the hospital rubbish look neat and tidy
options.D: To allow patients to help clean their own rooms

explanation: Sorting waste right away keeps sharp objects and dirty materials contained, protecting both staff and patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: What psychological challenge do patients in isolation face the most?
explanation: Being away from family and friends is tough. Isolation can make patients feel very lonely and worried. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h7)

question: How can you, as a nurse, best reduce feelings of loneliness for an isolated patient?

options.A: By keeping the isolation room lights turned off all day
options.B: By restricting all phone calls and family visits permanently
options.C: By engaging in friendly conversation beyond clinical tasks
options.D: By minimizing verbal communication to save time

explanation: A warm chat goes a long way! Taking a extra minute to talk helps break up the quiet and brightens their day. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h7)

question: What is one of the main duties of a nurse working in an isolation ward?

options.A: Designing new blueprints for isolation rooms
options.B: Procuring all financial grants for the hospital
options.C: Manufacturing hospital disinfectants and cleaning agents
options.D: Monitoring compliance with infection control protocols

explanation: You act as the safety champion! Nurses make sure everyone—staff, patients, and visitors—follows the infection rules. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)

question: Why must nurses teach family visitors the isolation rules before they step inside?

options.A: To test the memory capacity of visiting relatives
options.B: To reduce the number of visiting hours legally
options.C: To stop visitors from bringing food to the hospital
options.D: To prevent visitors from carrying pathogens out into the community

explanation: Informed visitors help stop germs from sneaking out of the hospital and into the outside community. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)
